acceptance.condition: Repository policy defaults are exactly Codex gpt-6-sol/medium and Antigravity gemini-3.8-flash/medium, and tests prove the policy remains the sole default authority with no adapter/carrier/workflow duplicate default constants.

Local run and continue, including continue delegation into PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and coding REPAIR, accept partial or complete Human model/effort overrides for Codex/Antigravity; direct canonical REMEDIATION and coding REPAIR surfaces preserve the same semantics. Omitted dimensions resolve deterministically, EXPLICIT versus REPOSITORY_DEFAULT attribution is preserved, and the exact resolved values reach native command construction.

A new authorization never implicitly inherits the previous RUN profile, while replay/restart/reconciliation of the same authorization reuses its exact bound profile even after repository defaults change.

PRIMARY remote carrier v3 validates one exact Human request, resolves one exact profile from canonical policy, propagates it through self-host delivery, and binds it into a new profile-aware durable PRIMARY dispatch identity before RUN native execution.

REMEDIATION intent v2 and REPAIR wakeup v2 provide the same exact request-resolution, workflow propagation, durable dispatch binding, idempotent replay, and changed-profile collision rejection guarantees as PRIMARY.

New profile-aware dispatch records and the eventual per-RUN execution-profile sidecar agree exactly on executor/model/effort/source attribution; any disagreement or invalid profile fails before native invocation.

Historical PRIMARY v1/v2, REMEDIATION v1, and REPAIR v1 durable journals remain readable/reconcilable under their exact historical semantics. Replaying or reconciling one of those existing identities does not resolve, attach, compare against, or persist current repository defaults, does not upgrade the journal version, and does not fabricate execution-profile provenance or a new native authorization. Newly submitted legacy carrier request versions are rejected rather than silently applying current defaults.

Invalid effort, malformed model identifier, missing required Executor/profile context, and profile options supplied to MiniMax invoke zero native Executors; MiniMax execution without profile options remains behaviorally unchanged.

A syntactically valid explicit alternate/future provider-native model identifier can flow end-to-end through local and remote profile binding without source-code registration or a global allowlist. Native provider rejection remains a no-fallback execution failure.

Remote operational receipts can retain bounded exact profile selectors where relevant without becoming lifecycle truth, and existing carrier receipts still avoid asserting RUN/verification/review/publication success from workflow completion alone.

Frozen TASK/RUN/RunLease/ExecutorBoundary semantics, Dispatcher exactly-one selection, sandbox/mutation authority, Runtime verification/EVIDENCE, Reviewer, Publisher, and no-retry/no-reroute boundaries remain unchanged.

Focused regression proves that after TASK-163 a compatible future default change can be expressed by editing only repository profile policy plus focused validation/smoke, with no required adapter, Dispatcher, Human carrier schema, durable dispatch schema, or lifecycle redesign. Adapter-mechanics regressions exercise explicitly injected profiles rather than duplicating the current repository default values as a second default authority.

Its execution-profile foundation, strict sidecar contract, immutable persisted-profile reuse, transport provenance, opaque model identifiers, and MiniMax isolation are the required implementation baseline and must not be redesigned.

docs/AIOS-EXECUTION-PROFILE-SELECTION.md is the Human-approved planning baseline. Human explicit selection outranks repository defaults; omitted values resolve from repository policy; every new PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, or REPAIR authorization resolves a fresh profile; restart/reconciliation of the same authorization reuses its exact already-bound profile.

Current new-request contracts on canonical main are PRIMARY wakeup request v2, REMEDIATION intent request v1, and REPAIR wakeup request v1. Current durable PRIMARY dispatch journal is profile-unaware v2 and REMEDIATION/REPAIR dispatch journals are profile-unaware v1. Historical records must remain readable and immutable.

Antigravity MiniMax remains outside Execution Profile management. Existing local MiniMax execution without model/effort override must remain supported, while model/effort override options must not be silently applied to MiniMax.

Runtime owns deterministic resolution/binding, admission, lifecycle reduction, verification, and evidence; Human owns explicit Executor/model/effort choice; Brain owns TASK semantics only; Executor owns implementation HOW; Reviewer and Publisher authorities remain unchanged.

hard: Activate exactly one repository-owned default authority by changing .ai/executor-profiles.yaml to Codex gpt-6-sol with medium effort and Antigravity gemini-3.8-flash with medium effort. Do not duplicate these defaults in adapters, carrier modules, workflows, CLI code, or tests as a second operational authority.

Human-facing local execution surfaces must accept optional exact model and effort overrides for profile-managed Codex/Antigravity execution, including run, continue, REMEDIATION, and coding REPAIR paths. Human explicit values override only the supplied dimension; omitted dimensions resolve from the repository policy. Explicit values that equal the current default remain attributed as EXPLICIT.

Omitted model/effort values must be resolved by deterministic repository code, never by Brain memory or carrier hard-coding. Model identifiers remain opaque bounded provider-native strings; reasoning effort remains validated against the selected Executor capability policy before native invocation.

Resolution is per new execution authorization. A new PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, or REPAIR authorization must resolve fresh defaults for omitted values and must not implicitly inherit the prior RUN profile. Restart, replay, or reconciliation of the same authorization must reuse the exact already-bound profile and must not re-resolve changed defaults.

New versioned remote requests must carry the Human-requested model and effort dimensions explicitly as present values or explicit absence/default intent. PRIMARY wakeup becomes request version 3, REMEDIATION intent becomes request version 2, and REPAIR wakeup becomes request version 2. Newly submitted legacy request versions must fail closed; historical legacy artifacts remain readable.

Remote carrier admission must deterministically resolve one exact profile from the Human request plus the canonical policy before self-host native execution. The exact executor, model, reasoning_effort, model_source, and effort_source must be propagated through the remote workflow boundary without later re-resolution or silent substitution.

New durable PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and REPAIR dispatch record versions must bind the exact resolved profile identity in addition to their existing selectors. Reuse of one dispatch identity with any changed executor/profile value or source attribution must fail closed before native invocation; exact replay must remain idempotent. Existing historical PRIMARY v1/v2, REMEDIATION v1, and REPAIR v1 journals must remain readable/reconcilable under their own historical binding, must never acquire retroactive profiles, and must never resolve or compare current repository defaults merely because a historical identity is replayed. If historical state lacks authority for safe continuation, fail closed rather than upgrading that authorization with a current profile.

When a RUN is created for a profile-managed execution, the persisted TASK-162 execution-profile sidecar must exactly match the profile bound by the local authorization or durable remote dispatch. Any mismatch, invalid effort, malformed profile selection, or conflicting persisted sidecar must invoke zero native Executors.

Operational receipts may expose the exact bounded profile selectors needed to diagnose remote delivery, but remain subordinate operational observations and must never claim RUN creation, native success, Runtime verification, semantic review, or publication beyond directly proven boundaries.

Human-supplied model/effort options without a valid profile-managed Executor must fail closed or return an executor-required Human surface without native invocation. Antigravity MiniMax execution without profile overrides remains unchanged; model/effort overrides must not be silently ignored or applied to MiniMax.

Provider-native unavailability or rejection of an exact syntactically valid model must remain an ordinary native execution failure. AIOS must not downgrade effort, replace the model, swap Executor, retry with another profile, or convert provider failure into deterministic validation policy.

Preserve TASK-162 future-evolution invariant: for an already-supported Executor with unchanged native invocation contract, a later compatible default model change must require only repository policy change plus focused validation/smoke. It must not require another carrier schema, Dispatcher, adapter, frozen RUN, or lifecycle redesign.

Tests that encode superseded pre-TASK-163 semantics for newly created authorizations, carriers, dispatch records, workflow forwarding, or current defaults must be migrated to the versioned profile-aware contract. Do not make production profile or dispatch validation permissive merely to preserve stale synthetic fixtures. Historical compatibility must be proven with explicitly constructed historical records/requests rather than by allowing a first-seen new authorization to omit required profile identity.
Do not modify files outside scope.modify and do not push or publish from Executor implementation.

task.goal: Implement Execution Profile Human Selection and Default Activation v1 on top of the published TASK-162 foundation. Allow the Human to select exact Codex or Antigravity model and/or reasoning effort per new execution authorization through local Human-facing CLI/continue and versioned PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and REPAIR remote delivery paths; resolve omitted values deterministically from the single repository-owned execution-profile policy; bind the exact resolved profile into new durable dispatch identity before native execution; preserve immutable per-RUN profile provenance and restart/reconciliation behavior; and activate the approved defaults Codex gpt-6-sol/medium and Antigravity gemini-3.8-flash/medium without creating routing, fallback, sticky profile state, or a second default authority.
non_goals: Change canonical TASK schema, frozen RUN schema, RunLease, ExecutorBoundary, Unified State lifecycle semantics, sandbox/mutation authority, Runtime verification/EVIDENCE, Reviewer verdict semantics, Publisher authority, or roadmap advancement.
Add automatic model routing, model scoring, task-difficulty classification, adaptive effort selection, fallback, retry, failover, Executor substitution, speculative execution, or multi-model voting.
Add a repository-global allowlist of provider model identifiers or require a code branch merely because a compatible provider-native model identifier is new.

Store a persistent Human preferred model/effort, create sticky inheritance across new authorizations, use conversation/model memory as default authority, or make Brain resolve omitted model/effort values.
Change Antigravity MiniMax native model semantics or bring MiniMax into the Codex/Antigravity Execution Profile policy.
Rewrite, migrate, backfill, reinterpret, or invalidate historical carrier requests, durable dispatch journals, RUNs, execution-profile sidecars, or terminal artifacts.

Require live provider availability, account entitlement, or network success as canonical deterministic verification. Native provider rejection of an exact requested model remains an execution failure and must not trigger fallback.
Modify Codex/Antigravity adapter command architecture or Dispatcher routing architecture solely to activate new defaults; TASK-162 already established exact injected-profile behavior.
Push or publish from Executor implementation execution.
task.problem: TASK-163 revision 1 correctly established the EP-2 target semantics, but its authored mutation authority was incomplete for the verification it required. RUN-163-003 reached Runtime verification with a clean, in-scope, repairable candidate and the first focused verification group failed because several dispatch tests still encoded pre-profile new-authorization contracts. Audit of the later required verification also found tests/test_codex_adapter.py and tests/test_antigravity_adapter.py still encoding the TASK-162 compatibility defaults even though revision 1 required the new repository defaults while leaving those two test files outside scope.modify. A correct revision-1 implementation therefore cannot update every required verification contract without violating TASK mutation authority. Revision 2 preserves the Human- approved Execution Profile activation intent, expands only the missing test mutation authority, requires stale synthetic tests to migrate to the strengthened profile-aware contracts rather than weakening production semantics, and tightens historical-journal compatibility so old authorizations are never reinterpreted through current defaults.
